haiku.good_for: exact edits, renames, sweeps over many files, grep and report, run a command and summarise

sonnet.good_for: a function or multi-file feature with a clear spec and a test, scripts, long reads

opus.good_for: root causes, risky review, hard multi-file work, design

fable.good_for: the hardest design and debugging, long-horizon planning
fable.weak_at: nothing that matters; it is the costliest

agy.good_for: bulk reading and summarising of files you name, first drafts, a second opinion; it uses its own quota, not your Claude quota
agy.weak_at: no view of this conversation, no verification, may invent details; Claude must check what it returns

codex.good_for: an independent review, a second implementation, code reading
codex.weak_at: no view of this conversation; Claude must check what it returns

gemini.good_for: reading long documents or logs, first drafts, a second opinion
gemini.weak_at: no view of this conversation; may invent details; Claude must check what it returns

rules: Grade the prompt before you read a file or run a command: split it into subtasks and pick a route for each. Write one line, Plan: <subtask> -> <pick>; ..., and make every subtask that is not stay-inline your FIRST action as an Agent call. The worker reads, edits and tests in its own context, so do not explore first.
Stay inline only for chat, a short answer, or a subtask of one or two tool calls on fewer than three files. Everything else goes to a worker.

Give each subtask the cheapest model and effort whose profile covers it: mechanical, well-specified work to the low end; work that needs judgement across connected files one or two steps up. Reading to answer a question, root causes, review and design stay inline, because the answer needs the whole conversation.
Open choices, answers that depend on this conversation, and synthesis stay inline or on a mid model. Risky work (money, auth, public API) gets a worker one step up, not a second look from you.

Batch: subtasks that suit the same model and effort go to ONE worker as a numbered list, not one worker each, because every worker call pays for its own setup. Independent batches go out together in one message.
Keep output short, yours and the workers': every worker is told to report under 150 words, and your own answer states the result and the check, nothing restated.
Start cheap. If the check fails, redo once one step up, never above the ceiling.
You keep judgement and the final answer. The worker's reported check output is the check. Do not re-read or re-review what it changed: that costs more than the worker did.
external_rules: An external AI uses its own quota, so what it reads costs you no Claude quota. Use one when the user names it, or when one job must read more than about 100k tokens (dozens of files, long logs): pass the files with --file and ask for a short answer, and do not read them yourself first. On a few small files the hand over costs about what it saves, so read those inline. Its output is a draft: skim it, then answer.
Do not send an external AI anything that needs this conversation, edits files, or is risky. If a call fails or the tool is out of quota, do the subtask yourself or on a worker.
